insights: Shorts drive virtually all channel views (median ~940 views vs 21.5 views for long-form), though long-form data is too thin (only 2 videos) to draw reliable conclusions on its format.

High retention does not guarantee Shorts feed pickup: the Submarine short had the highest retention (80.08%) but only 43 views because it failed to hit the Shorts algorithm (only 5% Shorts feed traffic vs 85-95% on 1,000+ view shorts).
Cutting-edge consumer tech and robotics (Tesla Roadster: 1,306, Quantinuum: 1,300, Unitree Robot: 1,081) consistently outperform space topics (NASA Mars short: 382 views).
Early hooks are leaking viewers: 4 out of 6 Shorts show sharp 5% to 9% drop-offs between 0 and 6.4 seconds, pointing to weak visual or verbal hooks in the opening line.
Subscriber conversion requires scale: only the top two videos crossing 1,300 views generated meaningful subscribers (+4 each), while all shorts below 1,000 views generated 0-1 subscribers.

Call-to-actions are failing completely: only 1 comment was generated across all 8 videos, indicating that current end-screen questions (like the 42.6s drop-off prompt in the Quantinuum short) are too abstract to trigger viewer replies.
